caption: An integer is its own numerator

wolfram.note: A deliberate divergence from Wolfram: it sends a factor to the denominator when its exponent has a negative leading coefficient, so (sin x - 2)^-b is denominator (sin x - 2)^b and the numerator is sin(x)^a. Ours moves only a factor with a negative number exponent, since b's sign is unknown: the whole product stays in the numerator.
sage.note: Sage, like Wolfram, sends a factor to the denominator when its exponent has a negative leading coefficient, so (sin x - 2)^-b goes to the denominator and the numerator is sin(x)^a. Ours moves only a factor with a negative number exponent, since b's sign is unknown: the whole product stays in the numerator.

julia.note: Nemo's ZZ takes an integer only; compute-engine's Numerator also takes a Gaussian integer or a list, which this mapping does not pass on.

wolfram.note: A deliberate divergence from Wolfram: it sends a^-b to the denominator (a negative leading coefficient in the exponent), so the numerator is 1 and the denominator a^b x. Ours moves only a factor with a negative number exponent, since b's sign is unknown: the numerator is a^-b.
sage.note: Sage, like Wolfram, sends a^-b to the denominator (a negative leading coefficient in the exponent), so the numerator is 1 and the denominator a^b x. Ours moves only a factor with a negative number exponent, since b's sign is unknown: the numerator is a^-b.
